JACKSON J. EVANS
Attorney

612-516-0682

October 28, 2026


VIA ELECTRONIC FILING

The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
Secretary
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street, N.E.
Washington, D.C. 20426

           Re:        ALLETE, Inc.
                      Docket No. ER27-___-000
                      Limited-Scope, Single Issue Section 205 Filing
                      Request for Acceptance of Depreciation Rates

Dear Secretary Reese:

        Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act, 1 and Part 35 of the Federal Energy
Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC” or “Commission”) regulations, 2 the Midcontinent
Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”), 3 on behalf of ALLETE Inc. (“ALLETE”), hereby
submits the proposed revised depreciation rates to be used when calculating ALLETE’s
transmission rates under Attachment O of MISO’s Tariff (“Attachment O”). As explained below,
ALLETE’s proposed depreciation rates have been accepted by the Minnesota Public Utilities
Commission (“MPUC”) for use in ALLETE’s retail rates for transmission, intangible, and general
plant assets, with the exception of general plant, Account 390. ALLETE expects the rates for
Account 390 to be approved by the MPUC. ALLETE did not request any changes for any of its
locations outside of accounting for the passing of one year’s time. 4

1
     16 U.S.C. § 824d.

2

3
     MISO joins this filing as the administrator of its Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff” or “MISO Tariff”)
     but takes no position on the substance of the filing and reserves the right to comment or protest.
4
     The MPUC has requested that ALLETE segregate its Account 390 by its major locations, for example the
     structures and improvements of ALLETE headquarters in Duluth, the various service centers, etc.

Sutherland. For a full description of the structure and a list of offices, please visit www.eversheds-sutherland.com.
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne Reese
October 28, 2026
Page 2

         ALLETE respectfully requests waiver of the Commission’s 60-day prior notice
requirement specified in Section 35.3 of the Commission’s regulations 5 to allow the proposed
depreciation rates to be effective January 1, 2026. 6 In the alternative, ALLETE requests that it be
allowed to make an adjustment during its 2026 Attachment O true-up (which will occur in June
2027) to recognize a January 1, 2026 effective date for accounting purposes to correspond with
the date the depreciation rates will become effective with the MPUC. 7 Further, ALLETE has
submitted their 2027 projection with the amendments proposed in this filing. To the extent the
Commission rejects the tariff amendments or the tariff amendments otherwise change in the course
of this proceeding, ALLETE will handle any adjustments, including refunds, through the True-Up
mechanism in the next Annual Update.

        ALLETE submits this request for authorization as a limited-scope or single-issue Section
205 filing. The Commission has explained that a single-issue Section 205 filing is appropriate
when a proposed rate change only impacts the timing of revenue collection, not the overall amount
of revenue recovered, such as with depreciation rates. 8 Therefore, ALLETE submits this request
for authorization to implement its state-approved depreciation rates as a limited scope or single-
issue Section 205 filing. ALLETE’s request is supported by several cases involving transmission
depreciation rates, including cases involving MISO Tariff, Attachment O - ALLETE. 9

II.       BACKGROUND

          A.       ALLETE

       ALLETE is an energy services company headquartered in Duluth, Minnesota. 11 ALLETE
implements its Minnesota franchised utility operations through Minnesota Power, a division of
ALLETE. Minnesota Power generates, transmits, and distributes electricity in a 26,000-square-
mile region of northern Minnesota, serving approximately 150,000 retail customers and providing
wholesale electric service to fourteen municipalities. Minnesota Power controls approximately
2,476 megawatts (“MW”) (summer and winter) of electric generation capacity through its
ownership of generation facilities and as a buyer under third-party power purchase agreements.

       Through Minnesota Power, ALLETE owns approximately 9,526 miles of electric
transmission and distribution lines and 149 substations. Minnesota Power has transferred
functional control of its alternating-current transmission facilities to MISO pursuant to the MISO
Transmission Owners Agreement and the MISO Tariff. 12

          MISO administers transmission-related services over ALLETE’s HVDC Facilities 13 as

III.       ALLETE’S PROPOSED DEPRECIATION RATES

           A.       ALLETE’s Proposed Depreciation Rates

        ALLETE’s currently effective transmission depreciation rates are included in ALLETE’s
MISO Attachment O Note Z Supplement (“Note Z Supplement”). These depreciation rates were
filed with the Commission on October 13, 2025, in Docket No. ER26-112-000 and accepted by
Letter Order issued December 9, 2025. 15

         This filing updates ALLETE’s currently effective Note Z Supplement depreciation rates.
ALLETE’s proposed depreciation rates have been accepted by the MPUC for use in ALLETE’s
retail rates for transmission, intangible, and general plant assets – except for general plant Account
390, which is pending at the MPUC – and fall into three categories of Accounts under 18 C.F.R.
Part 101:

                •   Transmission Plant: Accounts 351–359
                •   Intangible Plant: Accounts 301–302
                •   General Plant: Accounts 391–398 and Account 390 16

       In Order No. 618, the Commission determined that utilities should use appropriate methods
of depreciation to “allocate in a systematic and rational manner the cost of property to the periods
during which the property is used in utility operations, i.e., over its estimated useful service life.”17
Notably, the Commission has specifically recognized that even in the case of “pure wholesale

sales, the Commission does not impose one single method for depreciation accounting,” 18 but
instead reviews a utility’s depreciation practices “on a case-by-case basis.” 19

        To support its proposed depreciation rates, ALLETE submits the testimony of Brandi K.
Winfield as Exhibit No. ALT-01 (“Winfield Testimony”), which describes the studies and
processes ALLETE used to set the depreciation rates for each category of Account above. 20 The
Winfield Testimony explains that each of ALLETE’s proposed depreciation rates allocate facility
costs “in a systematic and rational manner” over the relevant facility’s service life and is consistent
with Order No. 618.

             1. Transmission Plant: Accounts 351-359, Intangible Plant: Accounts 301–302,
                and General Plant: Accounts 391–398

        The Winfield Testimony explains that the proposed depreciation rates for Accounts 351–
359, 301–302, and 391–398 were determined using the 2026 Annual Intangible, Transmission,
Distribution, and General Plant Depreciation Study filed with the MPUC in Docket No. E015/D-
26-166 on April 1, 2026 (“2026 ITDG Filing”). 21 The filing has not yet been approved by the
MPUC, however the Minnesota Department of Commerce recommended approval on September
2, 2026. These rates would be effective January 1, 2026. 22 The Winfield Testimony also explains
the factors affecting the determination of depreciation rates and lives for these accounts and the
calculations of depreciation expense and rates in the 2026 ITDG Filing.

        Appendix I of the 2026 ITDG Filing reflects ALLETE’s recommended depreciation rates
for all ALLETE intangible, transmission, distribution, and general plant depreciable property. 23
Non-depreciable property is not included in the 2026 ITDG Filing.

       ALLETE submits that the proposed depreciation rates for Accounts 351–359, 301–302,
and 391–398, as supported by the 2026 ITDG Filing, satisfy the requirements of Order No. 618
and other governing precedent 24 because they systematically and rationally allocate the cost of

                2. General Plant: Account 390

        The Winfield Testimony explains that the proposed depreciation rates for Account 390 are
based on ALLETE’s 2026 Annual Remaining Life Depreciation Filing made at the MPUC in
Docket No. E015/D-26-327 on September 1, 2026 (“2026 Remaining Life Filing”), 26 the filing
has not yet been approved. ALLETE expects the Account 390 rates to be approved by the MPUC.
Changes were requested, but they are not expected to be contested. 27 These rates would be
effective January 1, 2026. 28

       In its 2026 Remaining Life Filing, ALLETE requested that the remaining lives for all
Account 390 assets be adjusted for one year’s passage of time (i.e., from 2025 to 2026). There are
no proposed changes to salvage rates for any Account 390 assets. As explained in the Winfield
Testimony to justify its request, ALLETE reviewed its remaining lives and salvage rates for the
relevant structures and improvements and also reviewed plant and accumulated depreciation
reserve balances. Based on this analysis, ALLETE determined that the current remaining lives
and salvage rates for Account 390 assets systematically and rationally allocate costs over
ALLETE’s Account 390 assets’ lives, as required by Order No. 618 and other governing
precedent. 29

           B.      The Proposed Note Z Supplement Depreciation Rates are Just and Reasonable

        ALLETE respectfully submits that the proposed depreciation rates included in the Note Z
Supplement for Accounts 351–359, 301–302, 391–398, and 390 systematically and rationally
allocate costs over ALLETE’s assets’ lives. Therefore, the proposed depreciation rates are just,
reasonable, and not unduly discriminatory and should be used for purposes of calculating
transmission rates under ALLETE’s Attachment O.

       Further, the continued use of ALLETE’s MPUC-approved depreciation rates will allow
ALLETE to synchronize, to the extent possible, the depreciation rates in both its Attachment O
and retail rates, which simplifies ALLETE’s depreciation accounting and avoids the burden and

IV.       REQUESTED EFFECTIVE DATE AND REQUEST FOR WAIVER

        Pursuant to Section 35.13(b)(2) of the Commission’s regulations, 31 ALLETE respectfully
requests that the proposed revisions to the depreciation rates be made effective January 1, 2026,
and pursuant to Section 35.11 of the Commission’s regulations, ALLETE requests waiver of the
prior notice requirement to permit this effective date. 32 Good cause exists for this waiver. 33

        To incorporate the proposed depreciation rates into ALLETE’s Attachment O for the 2026
rate year, those rates will need to be effective January 1, 2026, subject to the true-up process in
ALLETE’s Attachment O protocols which will occur in June 2027.

       Granting the requested waiver would also promote consistency in the depreciation rates
used for federal and state ratemaking purposes, and avoid discrepancy between ALLETE’s state
mandated depreciation rates and ALLETE’s depreciation rates used for Attachment O-ALLETE.

        In the alternative, if the Commission does not grant waiver of the 60-day prior notice period
to allow ALLETE’s proposed formula rate changes to be effective January 1, 2026, ALLETE
respectfully requests that it be allowed to make an adjustment during its 2026 Attachment O true-
up process, which will occur in June 2027, to recognize January 1, 2026, as the effective date for
its depreciation rates. This request is consistent with the Commission’s finding in Southwest Power
Pool, Inc., where the Commission allowed depreciation rates that were updated for accounting
purposes to be reflected in a formula rate true-up. 34

V.       ADDITIONAL INFORMATION REQUIRED BY SECTION 35.13 OF THE
         COMMISSION’S REGULATIONS

         A.       Contents of Filing – Section 35.13(b)(1)

         ALLETE provides the following materials for filing:

              •   This transmittal letter;
              •   Tab A – Redline Attachment O ALLETE Depreciation Rates 35;
              •   Tab B – Clean Attachment O ALLETE Depreciation Rates;
              •   Exhibit ALT-01 – Winfield Testimony;
              •   Exhibit ALT-02 – 2026 ITDG Filing;
              •   Exhibit ALT-03 – 2026 Remaining Life Filing – Public Version
              •   Exhibit ALT-04 – 2026 ITDG Filing – Appendix I – 2026 ITD&G Depreciation
                  Rates; and
              •   Exhibit ALT-05 – 2026 ITDG Filing – Appendix II – 2025 Plant Reserve Expense.
              •   Exhibit ALT-06 – 2026 Rmn Life Appendix A1-A6

         B.       The Name and Address of Persons to Whom a Copy of the Rate Change Has
                  Been Posted – Section 35.13(b)(3)

        MISO has served a copy of this filing electronically, including attachments, upon all Tariff
Customers, MISO Members, Member representatives of Transmission Owners and Non-
Transmission Owners, MISO Advisory Committee participants, as well as all state commissions
within the region. The filing has been posted electronically on MISO’s website at:
https://www.misoenergy.org/legal/ferc-filings/ for other parties interested in this matter.

         C.       Brief Description of Rate Change – Section 35.13(b)(4)

     Section III above and the Winfield Testimony provides a detailed description of
ALLETE’s proposed depreciation rates.

         D.       Statement of Reason for Rate Change – Section 35.13(b)(5)

        As explained in Section III above, ALLETE is making this filing to update its depreciation
rates to be used in its Attachment O formula rates.

         E.       Requisite Agreement for Rate Change – Section 35.13(b)(6)

         As explained in Section III above, ALLETE is making this filing to update its depreciation

rates to be used in its Attachment O formula rates.

          F.       Statement Showing Expenses or Costs Included in Cost-of-Service Statements
                   – Section 35.13(b)(7)

       None of the costs related to this filing have been alleged in any administrative or judicial
proceeding to be illegal, duplicative, or unnecessary costs that are demonstrably the product of
discriminatory practices.

        ALLETE believes that it has provided sufficient information for the Commission to
evaluate the proposed depreciation rates. To the extent that this filing does not contain information
otherwise required for technical compliance with the Commission’s regulations, ALLETE
respectfully requests that compliance with such regulation be waived. 36 As noted, the Commission
generally permits single-issue filings regarding depreciation rates. 37

VI.       CONCLUSION

        ALLETE respectfully requests that the Commission accept the proposed depreciation rates
effective January 1, 2026.

 1   Q1.   PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME, POSITION, AND BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 2   A1.   My name is Brandi K. Winfield, and I am the Supervisor of Accounting for ALLETE, Inc.

 3         (“ALLETE”). My business address is 30 West Superior Street, Duluth, MN 55802.

 4

 5   Q2.   PLEASE DESCRIBE YOUR EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS.

 6   A2.   I am the supervisor of the property accounting department at ALLETE and have held this

 7         role since early 2024. I have 19 years of experience in accounting. I earned an Associate

 8         degree in accounting from Northwood Technical College in 2005, a Bachelor degree in

 9         accounting from the University of Wisconsin-Superior in 2013, and I have the professional

10         designation of Certified Public Accountant, which is currently active. I began my career

11         at AMSOIL INC. (“AMSOIL”) in 2007 as an accounts payable specialist and held several

12         other roles in the AMSOIL accounting department before moving to ALLETE in 2013 as

13         an Accounting Analyst in the property and construction accounting (“property

14         accounting”) department. In 2023, I worked in the general accounting department before

15         being promoted to my current role in early 2024 as the supervisor of the property

16         accounting department.

 5             Note Z Supplement to ALLETE’s MISO Attachment O (“Note Z Supplement”). My

 6             testimony supports ALLETE’s proposed depreciation rates in several ways. First, I present

17             Attachment O. The depreciation rates supported by the 2026 ITDG Filing and approved

7    Q4.       WHY IS ALLETE MAKING THIS FILING NOW?

8    A4.       ALLETE filed its current depreciation rates (and the associated supporting studies) with

9              the Commission on October 13, 2025, in Docket No. ER26-112-000. These rates were

20             tariff pages, Tab A and B, and Exhibit Nos. ALT-02 through ALT-06.

 1         1A.    Tab A and Tab B provide redline and clean copies of ALLETE’s proposed

 2                depreciation rates to be used in the Note Z Supplement of ALLETE’s Attachment

 3                O transmission formula rate, effective January 1, 2026.

 4         2A.    Exhibit ALT-02 is the 2026 ITDG Filing and supports ALLETE’s proposed

 5                depreciation rates for Accounts 301-302, 351-359, and 391-398.

 6         3A.    Exhibit ALT-03 is the 2026 Remaining Life Filing and supports ALLETE’s

 7                proposed depreciation rates for Account 390.

 9                2026 ITDG Filing.

11                Remaining Life Filing.

12

13                              ACCOUNTS 301-302, 351-359, AND 391-398

14   Q6.   PLEASE PROVIDE A SUMMARY OF THE 2026 ITDG FILING.

15   A6.   The 2026 ITDG Filing is ALLETE’s submission to the MPUC to establish or update the

16         depreciation values used in ALLETE’s current MPUC state-jurisdictional end-use

17         customer rates (as established in 2025) used in ALLETE’s retail rates (“MPUC Rates”).

18         The filing supports the depreciation expense and depreciation rates applicable to

19         ALLETE’s intangible, transmission, distribution, and general plant assets.

20         In a typical annual update, ALLETE updates its depreciation rates to reflect the passage of

21         one year and to include additions and retirements that impact the average remaining lives

22         and depreciation rates. This would leave the average service lives, net salvage rates, and

23         retirement curves unchanged from those approved in ALLETE’s last five-year 2021



                                                    5
                                                                             ALLETE, Inc. – Exhibit ALT-01
                                                                                Docket No. ER27-___-000

 1             Intangible, Transmission, Distribution, and General Plant Depreciation Petition filed with

 2             the MPUC in Docket No. E015/D-21-229 (“2021 ITDG Filing”) on April 1, 2021 and

 3             approved on August 2, 2021, which were the basis of ALLETE’s Attachment O

 4             depreciation rates for 2021 and used for the 2021 through 2024 rate years.

 5             The 2026 ITDG filing is also ALLETE’s five-year study. Accordingly, in addition to

 6             reflecting current plant and reserve information, the filing reevaluates the underlying

 7             average service lives, retirement curves, and net-salvage assumptions used to establish

 8             depreciation rates. The five-year study will be discussed further in questions 9 through 11

 9             below.

10             The depreciation rates included in the 2026 ITDG Filing are used to determine depreciation

11             expense for all the intangible, transmission, distribution, and general plant assets used in

12             ALLETE’s Attachment O for rate year 2026 (i.e., effective January 1, 2026– December

13             31, 2026). 10 The 2026 ITDG Filing establishes a systematic and rational allocation of costs

14             over the relevant facilities’ service lives for purposes of ALLETE’s Attachment O. 11

15

16   Q7.       WHAT FACTORS AFFECT THE DETERMINATION OF DEPRECIATION

17             RATES AND LIVES FOR THESE ACCOUNTS?

18   A7.       A number of factors, in addition to the passage of time, affect depreciation rates and

19             average remaining lives. These factors include additions, retirements, transfers, and

20             adjustments to plant; recorded depreciation; gross salvage; gains and losses; cost of


     10
           Non-depreciable property and Account 390-Structures and Improvements are not included in the 2025 ITDG
           Filing. The only rates relevant to ALLETE’s Attachment O are those for ALLETE’s intangible, transmission,
           distribution, and general plant assets.

     11
           Order No. 618 at 31,694.



                                                            6
                                                              ALLETE, Inc. – Exhibit ALT-01
                                                                 Docket No. ER27-___-000

 1   removal; and the resulting changes in gross plant, accumulated depreciation reserve, and

 2   the unaccrued balance.

 3   Plant additions and retirements can affect an account’s average remaining life differently

 4   depending on the age of the property involved. If there were no changes in gross plant, an

 5   account’s average remaining life generally would decrease by one year. However,

 6   additions of newer property may offset or exceed that one-year decrease and increase the

 7   account’s average remaining life. Similarly, retirement of older property may increase the

 8   average remaining life of the property that remains in service, while retirement of newer

 9   property may decrease it. As a result, an account’s average remaining life may decrease by

10   less than one year, remain unchanged, or increase from one year to the next.

11   Changes in the depreciation reserve relative to changes in plant also affect the unaccrued

12   balance and, therefore, annual depreciation expense and depreciation rates. The unaccrued

13   balance represents the remaining amount to be recovered through future depreciation

14   accruals, after considering the accumulated depreciation reserve and estimated net salvage.

15   If the unaccrued balance increases, more dollars generally remain to be allocated over the

16   account’s remaining life, which may increase annual depreciation expense and the

17   depreciation rate. Conversely, if the unaccrued balance decreases, fewer dollars generally

18   remain to be allocated, which may decrease annual depreciation expense and the

19   depreciation rate.

20   In a typical annual update, these factors are reflected using updated plant and reserve data

21   while applying the average service lives, survivor curves, and net-salvage rates approved

22   in the most recent five-year study. In a five-year ITDG Study, the analysis also considers

23   whether those underlying average service lives, retirement dispersion patterns or survivor



                                              7
                                                                      ALLETE, Inc. – Exhibit ALT-01
                                                                         Docket No. ER27-___-000

 1         curves, and net-salvage assumptions continue to reasonably reflect the expected future

 2         retirement and salvage characteristics of the property.

 3

 4   Q8.   HOW WERE DEPRECIATION EXPENSES AND RATES CALCULATED IN THE

 5         2026 ITDG FILING? WHY ARE THE 2026 ITDG FILING DEPRECIATION

 6         RATES SYSTEMATIC AND RATIONAL?

 7   A8.   ALLETE calculated annual and accrued depreciation using the straight-line, broad group,

 8         remaining-life depreciation method. In this system, the annual depreciation expense for

 9         each asset group is computed by dividing the original cost of the asset group less allocated

10         depreciation reserves less estimated net salvage by its respective average remaining life.

11

12         In an annual update, Alliance updates the average remaining lives and depreciation rates

13         using plant and reserve balances as of December 31 of the prior year, by vintage year

14         provided by ALLETE. The updated plant balances incorporate any additions, retirements,

15         transfers, and adjustments that occurred during the year. The updated reserve balance

16         incorporates recorded depreciation provision, retirements, transfers, adjustments, gross

17         salvage, gains, losses, and cost of removal during the current year. Then the approved

18         average service lives, net salvage rates and retirement curves from the most recent five-

19         year study are used to determine the average remaining lives by vintage within each FERC

20         account.

21         In contrast, a five-year ITDG study includes the updated plant and reserve information and

22         also reevaluates the underlying depreciation parameters themselves. Based on the asset

23         lives, retirement patterns, and net salvage analyses, changes may be recommended to the



                                                    8
                                                                       ALLETE, Inc. – Exhibit ALT-01
                                                                          Docket No. ER27-___-000

 1            average service lives, survivor curves, net salvage rates, or other related assumptions.

 2            Thus, the depreciation rate changes in a five-year filing may result from normal annual

 3            plant and reserve activity and from revised study findings.

 4            This filing updates the depreciation rates filed in Docket No. ER26-112-000. Specifically,

 5            ALLETE is proposing to further update the depreciation rates for Accounts 301-302, 351-

 6            359, and 391-398 based on the 2026 ITDG Filing and to reflect the passage of another year

 7            based on the 2026 Remaining Life Filing.

 8            The 2026 ITDG Filing is ALLETE’s five-year study, which was performed on behalf of

 9            ALLETE by Alliance. For this filing, ALLETE and Alliance used plant and reserve

10            balances as of December 31, 2025 by vintage year. The updated plant balances incorporate

11            any additions, retirements, transfers, and adjustments that occurred during 2025. 12 The

12            updated reserve balance incorporates recorded depreciation provision, retirements,

13            transfers, adjustments, gross salvage, gains, losses, and cost of removal in 2025.

14            The updated plant and reserve data, together with the average service lives, survivor curves,

15            and net salvage rates selected in the 2026 ITDG study were used to determine average

16            remaining lives by vintage within each applicable FERC account. The resulting average

17            remaining lives were then used to calculate the annual depreciation expense and rate. 13

18            Based on the above, these depreciation rates allocate facility costs “in a systematic and

19            rational manner” over the relevant facility’s service life consistent with FERC Order No.

20            618. 14

     13
          See id.

     14
          See supra note 5.



                                                       9
                                                                       ALLETE, Inc. – Exhibit ALT-01
                                                                          Docket No. ER27-___-000

 1

 2   Q9.    PLEASE PROVIDE A SUMMARY OF THE FIVE-YEAR 2026 ITDG STUDY

 3   A9.    The 2026 ITDG Study is a forward-looking analysis performed to develop depreciation

 4          rates for ALLETE’s depreciable intangible, transmission, distribution, and general plant

 5          property as recorded in ALLETE’s books and records as of December 31, 2025. The study

 6          is conducted at least every five years.

 7          The study evaluates depreciation parameters for property by the applicable FERC account

8           under the Commission’s Uniform System of Accounts, 18 C.F.R. Part 10112. It includes a

 9          remaining-life analysis, an evaluation of average service lives and retirement curves, a net-

10          salvage analysis, and the calculation of corresponding depreciation rates. Non-depreciable

11          property and Account 390—Structures and Improvements are excluded from the study.

12          The 2026 ITDG Study provides the basis for updating the depreciation rates used in

13          ALLETE’s MPUC Rates and, as applicable, in its Attachment O. Its appendices present

14          the recommended depreciation rates, average service lives, survivor curves, net-salvage

15          assumptions, depreciation-expense comparisons, and supporting net-salvage analysis by

16          account.

17

18   Q10. WHAT           METHODOLOGY                  WAS      USED        TO       DEVELOP           THE

19          RECOMMENDATIONS IN THE FIVE-YEAR 2026 ITDG STUDY?

20   A10.   The depreciation consultant conducted the 2026 ITDG Study in four principal phases.

21          First, the consultant collected and validated historical plant, reserve, retirement, and related

22          data from ALLETE’s property records, general ledger, construction or project systems,

23          fixed-asset systems, and other relevant operating-system interfaces. The consultant also



                                                       10
                                                              ALLETE, Inc. – Exhibit ALT-01
                                                                 Docket No. ER27-___-000

 1   conducted interviews with appropriate ALLETE accounting, engineering, and operations

 2   personnel to understand the characteristics, use, and expected future operation of the

 3   property.

 4   Second, the consultant performed life analyses using available historical data. Where

 5   sufficient vintage and retirement data were available, the consultant used actuarial

 6   retirement-rate analysis to develop observed life tables and assess the mortality

 7   characteristics of the property. Where historical data were insufficient to develop actuarial

 8   life estimates, the consultant used a simulated plant record (“SPR”) analysis. The SPR

 9   analysis applies selected survivor curves and average service lives to historical additions

10   and compares the resulting simulated balances to actual balances using graphical and

11   statistical comparisons.

12   Third, the consultant evaluated the historical analyses together with operational

13   information, anticipated changes in technology or system operations, property

14   characteristics, and other relevant considerations. Based on that evaluation, the consultant

15   selected the recommended average service lives, survivor curves or retirement dispersion

16   patterns, and net-salvage assumptions.

17   Finally, the consultant calculated the depreciation accrual rates, developed its

18   recommendations, and documented its conclusions in the 2026 ITDG Study.

19   The study necessarily incorporates informed professional judgment. Historical data are an

20   important input, but depreciation parameters also require consideration of the nature of the

21   property, ALLETE’s operating practices, industry and technology trends, expected

22   retirement patterns, and the reasonableness of the results as a whole.




                                              11
                                                                       ALLETE, Inc. – Exhibit ALT-01
                                                                          Docket No. ER27-___-000

 1   Q11. PLEASE          EXPLAIN          THE       SURVIVOR           CURVES,      NET-SALVAGE

 2          ASSUMPTIONS, AND CALCULATION OF DEPRECIATION RATES USED IN

 3          THE FIVE-YEAR 2026 STUDY.

 4   A11.   Individual assets within a group do not normally have identical lives or investment

 5          amounts. The average life of a group can be determined by comparing actual experience

 6          against various survivor curves. A survivor curve represents the percentage of property

 7          remaining in service at various age intervals. The most widely used set of representative

 8          survivor curves are the Iowa Curves. The Iowa Curves are the result of an extensive

 9          investigation of life characteristics of physical property made at Iowa State College

10          Engineering Experiment Station in the first half of the twentieth century. Through common

11          usage, revalidation, and regulatory acceptance, these curves have become a descriptive

12          standard for the life characteristics of industrial property.

13          A survivor curve pattern was selected based on analyses of historical data, as well as other

14          factors, such as general changes relevant to ALLETE’s operations. The blending of

15          judgment concerning current conditions and future trends, along with the matching of

16          historical data permits the depreciation analyst to make an informed selection of an

17          account's average life and retirement dispersion pattern. Iowa Curves were used to depict

18          the estimated survivor curves for each account.

19          In the 2026 ITDG Study, the consultant used historical retirement information, where

20          available, together with SPR analysis, operational information, and informed judgment to

21          select the survivor curve and average service life that best represented the expected future

22          retirement characteristics of each account or property group.




                                                      12
                                                                        ALLETE, Inc. – Exhibit ALT-01
                                                                           Docket No. ER27-___-000

 1          The study also evaluated net salvage. Net salvage is the difference between gross salvage—

 2          the residual or sale value received when property is retired—and the cost of removing and

 3          disposing of that property. Because retirement and removal activities may produce either

 4          positive or negative net salvage, the net-salvage assumptions reflect the consultant’s

 5          analysis of historical experience and expected future conditions.

 6          Using the selected life, curve, and net-salvage parameters, the consultant calculated

 7          depreciation rates under the straight-line, broad-group, remaining-life method. The

 8          calculation allocates the remaining undepreciated investment, adjusted for estimated net

 9          salvage and accumulated depreciation reserve, over the estimated average remaining life

10          of the applicable property group. The resulting rates provide a systematic and rational

11          allocation of the costs of the applicable facilities over their service lives.

12

13                                                 ACCOUNT 390

14   Q12. WHAT IS THE SUPPORT FOR ALLETE’S PROPOSED DEPRECIATION

15          RATES FOR ACCOUNT 390?

16   A12.   As explained in Docket No. ER26-112-000, ALLETE’s current Account 390 rates are

17          based on ALLETE’s 2020 Annual Remaining Life Depreciation Filing made at the MPUC

18          in Docket No. E-015/D-20-701 on September 1, 2020 and approved on March 24, 2021.

19          These rates were updated at the MPUC in ALLETE’s 2026 Remaining Life Filing.

20          The proposed depreciation rates for Account 390 used for purposes of ALLETE’s

21          Attachment O in this filing are computed in a manner consistent with ALLETE’s 2025




                                                       13
                                                                              ALLETE, Inc. – Exhibit ALT-01
                                                                                 Docket No. ER27-___-000

 1            Remaining Life Filing that was approved by the MPUC, 15 updated in the 2026 Remaining

 2            Life Filing 16 currently pending approval with the MPUC. For Account 390, ALLETE is

 3            requesting that the remaining lives of all Account 390 facilities be adjusted for one year’s

 4            passage of time. For all 390 locations there are no proposed changes to salvage rates.

 5

 6   Q13. HOW IS ALLETE PROPOSING TO USE DEPRECIATION RATES FILED WITH

 7            THE MPUC IN ITS ATTACHMENT O TO ADDRESS REGULATORY LAG?

 8   A13.     As stated above, ALLETE is proposing to use its currently effective MPUC depreciation

 9            rates that allocate facility costs “in a systematic and rational manner” over the relevant

10            facility’s service life consistent with FERC Order No. 618 in its MISO Attachment O.
